h: Mansions, Hills and the Howe of Fife
p: The Howe of Fife is the broad, fertile valley of the River Eden, and it's a lovely quiet corner of Scotland to explore at a slow pace. Fife Zoo sits right in the middle of it, which means everything else is close by.

Just south of Cupar, Hill of Tarvit Mansion is a grand Edwardian house run by the National Trust for Scotland, with formal gardens and woodland walks. On the other side of the valley, the Lomond Hills rise above Falkland, and the climb up East Lomond is a manageable walk for older kids with views over half of Fife. Falkland Palace was a favourite hunting retreat of the Stuart kings and has one of the oldest real tennis courts in the world still in use.

Cupar itself is the old county town of Fife, a handsome place with a mercat cross and independent shops and cafés, handy for lunch. Head east and you reach St Andrews, with its ruined cathedral, castle and long West Sands beach, while Tentsmuir Forest, near Tayport, has pine woods and a wild beach where seals are often seen hauled out on the sandbanks.

Practical tip: both Cupar and Ladybank have railway stations on the line between Edinburgh and Dundee, but the zoo is out in the countryside, so a car or taxi makes life much easier. Wellies are a good shout after rain.
